metadata.title: Content Strategy Isn't Writing Your Posts.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude 'does content strategy,' does it write your posts, or does it rank what's actually selling first? Lands the carry-out that the skill stops at a ranked, owner-approved brief -- writing the posts is a separate, later step.
metadata.anchor_pair: N/A — source is skill-teardown format (anatomy -> pipeline -> constraint -> verdict), no anchor structure to preserve

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes this skill writes their social posts for them. It doesn't — it reads actual sales data from QuickBooks, PayPal, or Square and ranks what's selling, what's slowing, and what's trending, before any post gets written.

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: This kind of work is built from something called a skill — a folder Claude reads before it acts. Inside is one file that spells out exactly how raw sales numbers turn into a plan: pull the data, rank it, weigh the season, write the brief. Claude reads the file, then follows it. The file is the whole program.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon opening to reveal SKILL.md, reference/gotchas.md, reference/examples/; SKILL.md highlighted

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens on cream to reveal three items: SKILL.md (highlighted in crimson), reference/gotchas.md, reference/examples/. A caption below reads 'Claude reads it, then follows it.'

beats.narration_text: The steps run in order: pull ninety days of sales data from QuickBooks, PayPal, or Square, rank it against seasonality, then hand back a thirty-day brief. Nothing skips ahead — the owner approves the brief before anything gets built from it.

shot.new_visual_element: Three-phase pipeline: Pull sales data -> Rank + weigh season -> Return brief for approval

production_viz.label: Data in, ranked brief out
production_viz.mechanic: Three cards left to right joined by arrows: 'Pull sales data', 'Rank + weigh season', 'Return brief for approval'. Linear, no branch points drawn.

beats.narration_text: The brief itself has six parts: an executive summary, what to push hard, what to hold steady, what to reposition or pause, seasonal opportunities coming up, and recommended offers. That's the entire output — no calendar, no captions, no images. Those wait for the owner's approval and a separate skill.

shot.new_visual_element: Six brief-section rows: executive summary, push hard, hold steady, reposition/pause, seasonal opportunities, recommended offers; a boundary line with 'no calendar. no assets.' beyond it

production_viz.label: Six sections, then it stops
production_viz.mechanic: Six rows fill in one at a time with a checkmark: 'Executive summary', 'Push hard', 'Hold steady', 'Reposition or pause', 'Seasonal opportunities', 'Recommended offers'. A dashed boundary line beneath the list, with a faint unlabelled field beyond it captioned 'no calendar. no assets.'

beats.narration_text: Content strategy here isn't Claude writing your posts — it's Claude reading your sales numbers and ranking what's working. It stops at the brief; building the posts is a separate step that needs your approval first.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. List your last month's top five sellers and slowest five — made-up numbers are fine. Ask Claude: rank these into what to push hard, what to hold steady, and what to reposition, and stop there, don't draft any actual posts yet. Liam, in for Bear.
